title: Curate critical console cards, defer deep tracing & cost drilldowns for initial MVP
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Reduce scope for the first Console release by shipping a tightly curated set of insights (cards) and lightweight tracing samples, deferring full trace explorer and deep cost drilldowns. This keeps customer-facing telemetry useful for most operational needs while controlling implementation cost and launch risk.

Background: Stakeholders requested dashboards, tracing, and cost breakdowns in the initial Console launch. Engineering capacity and cost constraints mean we cannot deliver full-feature parity (deep interactive trace explorer + per-tag cost rollups) without delaying the release. This ticket documents the accepted cuts, the rationale, and acceptance criteria for the trimmed MVP.

Out-of-scope for MVP (explicit cuts):
- Interactive trace explorer with request-level waterfall and per-span timeline (deferred to post-MVP).
- Arbitrary tag-driven cost drilldowns (deferred).
- Full historical cost heatmaps beyond 7 days.
- Route-level cohort comparisons and A/B foldouts.

In-scope for MVP (minimum viable deliverables):
- Curated dashboard deck containing: 1) Route summary card (requests, errors, p50/p95 latency), 2) Top-5 cost-by-route card (7-day window), 3) Token usage and per-token cost estimate card, 4) Error-trend mini-card.
- Lightweight tracing sample pipeline: 1% sampling by default with ability to toggle 5% for canary customers; sampled traces surfaced as a simple list with timestamp, route, latency, and link to raw trace JSON for download. No waterfall visualization in-MVP.
- Cost inspector: aggregated cost buckets (model compute, embeddings, storage) and a drillable top-5 routes list (no arbitrary filters).
- Rollout feature flag and gated enablement for internal beta customers.

Rationale and trade-offs:
- Trade reduced interactivity for faster delivery and lower infra costs. Customers lose immediate per-request drilling, but retain high-level operational signals to triage issues and identify high-cost routes.
- Mitigations include: raw trace download for engineers, prioritized backlog tickets for trace explorer and cost filter UX, and a small docs/diagnostics playbook to help SREs debug without full explorer.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Dashboard deck is visible to users with Console access and contains the four required cards (route summary, top-5 cost-by-route, token usage, error trend).
2) Each card updates at the cadence specified in the PRD (route summary and error trend: 1m; cost and token usage: 15m).
3) Lightweight trace sampling pipeline is operational: sampled traces appear within 30s of ingestion, sample rate configurable via feature flag (1% default, 5% toggle).
4) Sampled-trace list shows timestamp, request-id, route, latency, status code and a working "Download raw trace" link that returns a JSON blob.
5) Cost inspector surfaces aggregate buckets and the top-5 routes for the selected time window (7d default) and the numbers reconcile with billing dashboard within 5%.
6) Built-in feature flag and rollout gating exist; internal beta orgs can opt-in before public launch.
7) Docs: short playbook published on Confluence with diagnostics steps for engineers (including how to get raw traces).
8) Smoke tests and e2e tests validate card rendering, trace download, and cost aggregation logic in CI; test results are green in the release branch.
updates: 2025-02-11: Initial scoping workshop with Eng (Marco Ruiz) and Design (Priya Kapoor). Agreement to prioritize route-level signals over full trace explorer.
2025-02-12: Product review — removed per-tag cost filters to reduce backend index requirements. Decision recorded in PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CONSOLE/Curate+Critical+Cards+MVP
2025-02-14: Engineering raised concern about token-cost reconciliation window; agreed to 15m aggregation for cost metrics to balance accuracy and query load (note added in PRD).
2025-02-16: Design delivered lightweight trace list mockups; no waterfall view in MVP. Mockup link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1TraceMockups
2025-02-17: Security review triage — no customer PII exposed in sampled traces; redaction rules documented. Security owner: Sanjay Patel (no full review required pre-MVP).
2025-02-18: Prepared rollout plan and feature-flagging spec. GH draft PR for frontend & API changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1287
review_feedback: Marco Ruiz (Eng): Prefer sampling over full ingestion for traces; asked for clear SLAs on sample-to-surface time.
Priya Kapoor (Design): Emphasize compact visual density on dashboard cards; requested microcopy for 'Download raw trace' to set expectations.
Amira N'Golo (Customer Success): Recommend enabling limited opt-in for 5% sampling for customers in our early access program to capture rare edge cases.
implementation_notes:
- Backend: implement aggregated cost query endpoints (7d, 24h) with pre-aggregation to limit load.
- Tracing: attach sampling hook at request ingress; store a compact trace document plus raw blob export.
- Frontend: card components with mobile-friendly collapse behavior.
- Ops: add alert if sampled trace queue latency > 2 minutes.
- Backlog: follow-up tickets for trace explorer (PM-395124) and cost-tag filters (PM-395125).
